authority_policy: current official manual overrides legacy sources

records.title: RouterOS REST API semantics
records.summary: RouterOS REST is a JSON wrapper over RouterOS API/CLI behavior. GET maps to print/read, PATCH to set/update, PUT to add/create, DELETE to remove, and POST can invoke console commands. HTTPS should be preferred; plain HTTP is lab-only because credentials can be exposed.
safety_rules: prefer www-ssl/HTTPS
do not embed credentials in URLs
writes require normal project admission and transaction gates

records.title: RouterOS native API
records.summary: The native API is intended for information gathering, configuration adjustment, and router management and closely follows CLI syntax. Secure API service is preferred for production use.
safety_rules: prefer secure transport
grant only the policies required by the selected micro-tools

records.title: Safe Mode and management survival
records.summary: Safe Mode is designed to reduce lockout risk. Configuration changes made while Safe Mode is active are automatically undone if the session terminates abnormally. The history is finite, so management-critical changes should be small and verified incrementally.
safety_rules: make management-critical changes in small verified batches
never treat Safe Mode as protection for reboot-required operations

records.title: Binary backup and text export
records.summary: RouterOS supports binary system backup and human-readable configuration export. Binary backups contain sensitive device configuration and should be encrypted and stored securely. Text export does not include every sensitive or auxiliary data set and should be treated as a complementary artifact, not a substitute for binary backup.
safety_rules: encrypt binary backups
record RouterOS version with every backup
keep sanitized export and binary backup as separate artifacts

records.title: Configuration management invariants
records.summary: RouterOS records configuration actions in system history and supports undo/redo, Safe Mode, export/import, reset, and backup/restore. Import/export compatibility depends on RouterOS command availability, so version provenance must be recorded with deployment artifacts.
safety_rules: record RouterOS version
verify idempotency before declaring deployment complete

records.title: Stateful firewall baseline
records.summary: RouterOS firewall supports stateful filtering through connection tracking. Established and related traffic can be recognized, invalid traffic should be dropped, and firewall/NAT policy must protect both the router input plane and forwarded LAN traffic.
safety_rules: preserve established/related return traffic
drop invalid state
deny unsolicited WAN access by default
separate router-input policy from forwarding policy

records.title: Management-plane hardening
records.summary: Router management exposed from WAN must be minimized and source-restricted. Interface identity matters: applying a rule to the wrong public interface can cause lockout or unintended exposure. Strong credentials, least privilege, logging, and current RouterOS are part of the hardening baseline.
safety_rules: deny WAN management unless explicitly required
restrict management sources
verify the actual WAN interface before applying policy

records.title: WireGuard peer routing and keepalive
records.summary: WireGuard allowed-address controls accepted source networks and peer-directed destinations; ranges cannot overlap on one interface. Persistent keepalive is used only when needed to keep a stateful firewall or NAT mapping alive. Handshake, RX/TX counters, and current endpoint are useful verification evidence.
safety_rules: reject overlapping allowed-address ranges
do not route Internet default through site-to-site VPN unless explicitly requested
verify a recent handshake and LAN-to-LAN reachability

records.title: Bridge VLAN filtering deployment order
records.summary: Bridge VLAN filtering controls VLAN-aware Layer-2 forwarding. VLAN membership and management access must be prepared before vlan-filtering is enabled because enabling it can filter traffic to the CPU and lock out management. Hardware-offload behavior varies by switch chip and RouterOS version.
safety_rules: configure management path before enabling vlan-filtering
enable vlan-filtering last
validate model/switch-chip capability before assuming hardware offload

records.title: Checkpoint backups during deployment
records.summary: MikroTik recommends creating backups after major configuration sections. Automation should therefore create versioned checkpoints around management-critical milestones instead of only taking one backup at the end.
safety_rules: create pre-change backup
create post-change verified backup
retain milestone metadata
